Applying Fixes

Learn how to safely apply automated code fixes with RoselineMCP.

Overview

The applyFixes tool automatically fixes code issues identified by analyzers. Always preview changes before applying.

Basic Usage

Preview Mode (Recommended First Step)

{
  "tool": "applyFixes",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core",
    "ids": ["CS0168"],
    "previewOnly": true
  }
}

Apply Fixes

{
  "tool": "applyFixes",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core",
    "ids": ["CS0168", "IDE0005"],
    "previewOnly": false
  }
}

Common Fix Scenarios

Remove Unused Code

{
  "ids": ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0051", "IDE0052", "RCS1213"]
}

Fix Code Style

{
  "ids": ["SA1101", "SA1200", "SA1210", "SA1309"]
}

Modernize Code

{
  "ids": ["IDE0017", "IDE0028", "IDE0031", "IDE0041", "IDE0090"]
}

Understanding the Response

{
  "project": "MyApp.Core",
  "fixesApplied": 15,
  "filesChanged": [
    "Services/UserService.cs",
    "Models/Product.cs"
  ],
  "patch": "--- a/Services/UserService.cs\n+++ b/Services/UserService.cs\n...",
  "appliedFixers": [
    {
      "diagnosticId": "CS0168",
      "fixerName": "Remove Unused Variable",
      "count": 8
    }
  ]
}

Safe Fix Workflow

  1. List diagnostics to identify fixable issues
  2. Preview fixes with previewOnly: true
  3. Review the patch to understand changes
  4. Apply fixes if satisfied
  5. Test your code after applying

Best Practices

  • Always preview first
  • Fix one diagnostic type at a time
  • Commit before applying fixes
  • Run tests after fixes
  • Review patches carefully
